item: The custody keys pill's hover says what the key files hold, for each protection value
summary: R484 item (3), after the ML-DSA key file change. The Chain of custody status pill 'keys: ...' had one hover for every install, 'Set OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE to encrypt keys at rest': wrong on an install whose keys are encrypted, and wrong on one encrypted by the database passphrase, which wraps the signing keys too. _KEY_PROTECTION_TIPS in app-ai-tools.js now holds one hover per value of HybridSigner.key_protection. aes256gcm-scrypt: the keys in use are encrypted under the passphrase, with the at-rest threat model. pkcs8-pbkdf2: an older form that is far cheaper to guess against, re-encrypted on each load unless its file cannot be replaced. plaintext-0600: unencrypted, encrypted when the app has the database passphrase or OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE, and if shown with one held, a key file could not be replaced (a read-only folder or a linked file) and each load tries again. The hovers say 'in use' because key_protection does not read an ML-DSA file while post-quantum signing is off (the docs/SECURITY.md stated limit). A value with no entry gets no hover rather than a wrong one. The three are keyed in the 12 locales and the old key is removed. tests/test_custody_key_pill.py pins the map against the values the signer's own source can return. Two USER_MANUAL lines that named only OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE now name the database passphrase too. Release-notes line: the custody keys pill's hover now says how the signing keys in use are stored, instead of always asking for OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE.
